source.citation: "Early Street Maps of Chicago." Chicagology. A gallery of reproduced early Chicago maps - Thompson 1830, the Kinzie manuscript map hand-dated 1833, Wright 1834, Wabonsia 1835, Andreas's 1830 landownership map, Wolf's Point 1853 and both states of the Conley/Stelzer map - with an uncredited editorial ADDENDUM on the town's first streets and roads.
what_it_does_not_supply: a date for Thomas Church's store
a block, lot or corner for it
usable reproductions of the maps it gathers - re-source from the holding institution
reliable bibliographic data for the Conley/Stelzer map
any citation whatever for its addendum
what_it_supplies: the existence of a first store building on Lake Street, a two-story frame structure, built by Thomas Church
the first Tremont House at the north-west corner of Dearborn and Lake, 1833
Lake Street as the main street of the town from 1833
South Water Street as the town's first street, "a muddy, narrow trail running east and west along the south bank"
the Milwaukee Trace / Northwest Plank Road and the Barry Point Trail and Nine-mile Swamp route out of town
a finding aid to the early Chicago map literature
Thompson 1830 street width 80 ft and alley width 18 ft, uncited
